full_judgment: 8. I have perused the materials on record and considered the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners with in depth reading of the reference given by him. 4 PWs and 4 DWs were examined who deposed supporting their respective sides. On further reading of the judgments of the Courts below in appeared to me that the trial Court framed 5 issues which were discussed and decided collectively in violation of municipal law and the appellate Court took one point which was not properly discussed. Both the Courts below very slipshod way discussed the statements of the witnesses and committed error to explain the Hindu Mitakhara law of inheritance arid appreciated the alleged will made by Sharashi Bala that could not be produced before any Court that the DS tenant Goshai Das and Thakur Das Shaha died leaving behind two sons namely, Gour Gobindha Shaha and Akhoy Kumar Shaha became the owner and possession of the suit hind by way inheritance. DS Parcha was also correctly recorded in their names and in amicable partitioned Gour Gobindha Shaha owned and posses 0.51 and 0.28 acre of land from Plot Nos. 877 and 702 respectively. Thereafter Gour Gobindha Shaha died leaving behind only one wife namely, Shaynashi Bala Shaha who transferred the land of plot No. 702 to one Azimuddin and in SA Khatian No. 635 was prepared in the name of Shornasi Bala Shaha showing an area of 0.81 acre of land of plot No. 877 and this Sharashi Bala made a will in favour of the defendant opposite parties on 12th Sraban, 1383 amounting to 0.51 acre of land from plot No. 877 and handed over the will to their and accordingly RS Parcha was also prepared in their names by opposite parties and the defendant opposite parties have been possessing the suit land. Thereafter Akhoy Kumar died leaving behind two sons namely. Ajit Shaha and Ranjit Shaha as inheritance and Ranjit died as no issue and the son of Ajit left for Bharat where he is now residing. The daughter of Akhay namely, Nirmala Shaha married with one Mehendra Shaha and their son are alive and there was no sister of Akhay and the plaintiffs petitioner are not the son of the sister of Akhoy. So they cannot claim the property as inherited property in accordance with Hindu law and dismissed the suit and the appeal. According to the Mitakhara law of inheritance Shurashi Bala, wife of late Gour Gobindha Shaha who executed the alleged will as only the life interest in the property left out by Gour Gobindha Shaha that the Courts below committed an error of law in not considering that Shurashi Bala Shaha had only life interest in the property left out by her husband Gour Gobindha Shaha and she had no transferable interest in the property of her husband. A Hindu widow has life interest in the estate of her deceased husband, she can transfer such property only on the valid legal necessity a transfer made by the widow without legal necessity is valid and binding only during the life of widow as provided under section 205 and after her death that the transfer will be invalid and the reversionary heirs will be entitled to the restoration of the said property and in this case the petitioners in the reversionary heirs of the said Gour Gobindha Shaha without considering the aspect the Courts below passed by the judgments which are not at all maintainable in law. The aforesaid discussion of Hindu law and the claim of the petitioners in the suit property had also support in the decisions of our apex Court as referred by the learned advocate for the petitioners and the same were also applicable in the instant rule. In view of the above the Courts below absolutely violated the Hindu Mitakhara law of inheritance that perversed both the judgments which need to be interfered with. The rule has merit.
